title: Preference-Optimized Retrieval and Ranking for Efficient Multimodal Recommendation

problem.claim: Multimodal recommendation needs to capture fine-grained user preferences while maintaining efficient inference.

gap.claim: Existing approaches largely rely on static item attributes and often treat retrieval and ranking as separate stages, limiting contextual modeling and joint optimization.

contributions.claim: PRIME combines a lightweight candidate retriever with an LMM ranker that uses user history and multimodal item features.
PRIME uses prompt-based preference modeling and verbalizer-based inference to support fine-grained ranking with one forward pass over candidates.
The LMM ranker provides feedback for online preference optimization, refining retrieval and improving retrieval-ranking alignment.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that PRIME captures subtle user intentions and ranks candidates efficiently with low inference cost.
The authors report that extensive experiments show consistent performance and efficiency gains over baseline methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Large multimodal models support textual and visual understanding and generation and have been applied to recommendation.
Prior methods underuse contextual item information and overlook interactions between retrieval and ranking.
PRIME retrieves candidates with a lightweight model and ranks them with an LMM using user history and multimodal features.
Verbalizer-based inference reduces ranking computation, while ranker feedback enables online preference optimization of the retriever.
The authors report improved intention capture, efficient ranking, and superior performance and efficiency relative to baselines.

source_observation.claim: A recommendation pipeline can jointly model candidate retrieval and downstream ranking instead of optimizing them independently.

interpretation.claim: Feedback from later-stage decisions may improve alignment between upstream selection and final preference modeling.

application.claim: Use ranker-generated feedback to refine retrieval candidates when retrieval quality and ranking quality are tightly coupled.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when online preference optimization is beneficial or what constraints it imposes.

source_observation.claim: Single-pass scoring and lightweight retrieval are used to reduce multimodal recommendation inference cost.

interpretation.claim: Efficiency can be improved by reducing both candidate-generation overhead and repeated ranking computation.

application.claim: For latency-sensitive ranking systems, combine a compact retriever with batched or single-pass candidate scoring.

exception.claim: The abstract does not quantify latency, cost, scalability, or possible accuracy trade-offs.

unknowns: Datasets, evaluation metrics, baseline identities, and numerical results are not specified.
The retriever, ranker, prompt design, verbalizer, and online optimization procedures are not described in implementation detail.
Ablations, limitations, deployment conditions, and independent verification are not provided.
